# Chapter 10: Feature Flags and Compatibility

One of the defining triumphs of the ext filesystem architecture is its ability to introduce major structural innovations over three decades without needlessly breaking compatibility with older kernel drivers.

A Linux 4.4 kernel from 2016 can mount a modern ext4 partition formatted in 2026, seamlessly ignoring features it does not recognize while safely refusing to execute operations that could corrupt on-disk state.

This backward and forward compatibility is governed by **Three Feature Flag Categories** embedded directly inside the primary superblock. This chapter details these feature bitmasks, analyzes critical runtime mount options, and demonstrates how to check and manipulate feature flags programmatically.

## The Three Feature Flag Categories

The ext4 superblock defines three 32-bit integer fields that govern how kernel drivers must interact with the volume:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        FEATURE COMPATIBILITY MATRIX                    │
│                                                                        │
│   Superblock Field        Behavior if Unknown Flag is Present          │
│   ───────────────────     ──────────────────────────────────────────   │
│   s_feature_compat        SAFE: Driver mounts Read-Write.              │
│                           Older driver ignores the unknown feature.    │
│   s_feature_ro_compat     SAFE READ-ONLY: Driver mounts Read-Only.     │
│                           Modifications could corrupt unknown feature. │
│   s_feature_incompat      UNSAFE: Driver REFUSES TO MOUNT entirely.    │
│                           On-disk structures cannot be safely read.    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. Compatible Features (`s_feature_compat` - Offset `0x5C`)
Features that older drivers can safely ignore without risk of data loss:
- `EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL` (`0x0004`): Volume possesses a valid JBD2 journal.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_EXT_ATTR` (`0x0008`): Extended attributes are present.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_RESIZE_INODE` (`0x0010`): Inode 7 reserved for online resize GDT expansion.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_DIR_INDEX` (`0x0020`): HTree directory indexing active.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_SPARSE_SUPER2` (`0x0200`): Backup superblocks stored only in two explicit groups.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FAST_COMMIT` (`0x0400`): Fast commit logging enabled in journal.

### 2. Read-Only Compatible Features (`s_feature_ro_compat` - Offset `0x64`)
An older kernel driver can safely read files from the disk, but must refuse to write to the filesystem:
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_SPARSE_SUPER` (`0x0001`): Sparse superblock distribution.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_LARGE_FILE` (`0x0002`): Files larger than 2 GiB present.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_HUGE_FILE` (`0x0008`): Inode `i_blocks` counts measured in filesystem blocks instead of 512-byte sectors.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_GDT_CSUM` (`0x0010`): Uninitialized block groups (`uninit_bg`).
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_DIR_NLINK` (`0x0020`): Directories with more than 65,000 subdirectories.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_EXTRA_ISIZE` (`0x0040`): Inodes larger than 128 bytes with extended timestamps.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_QUOTA` (`0x0100`): In-tree hidden quota tracking active.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_METADATA_CSUM` (`0x0400`): Full CRC32c metadata checksumming active.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_PROJECT` (`0x2000`): Project quota tracking active.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_RO_COMPAT_VERITY` (`0x8000`): Read-only files with `fs-verity` Merkle trees.

### 3. Incompatible Features (`s_feature_incompat` - Offset `0x60`)
The on-disk format has changed fundamentally. An older driver lacking support must refuse to mount the filesystem:
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_FILETYPE` (`0x0002`): Directory entries contain `file_type` byte.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_RECOVER` (`0x0004`): Volume needs journal recovery before mounting.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_EXTENTS` (`0x0040`): Inodes use B+ extent trees instead of indirect blocks.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_64BIT` (`0x0080`): Group descriptors are 64 bytes wide; 48-bit block addressing.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_FLEX_BG` (`0x0200`): Flexible block groups (bitmaps clustered together).
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_EA_INODE` (`0x0400`): Large extended attributes stored in dedicated external inodes.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_INLINE_DATA` (`0x2000`): Small files embedded directly inside inodes.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_ENCRYPT` (`0x10000`): Directory encryption (`fscrypt`) active.
- `EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_CASEFOLD` (`0x20000`): Case-insensitive directories enabled.

## Mount Options and Their Effects

Filesystem behavior can be dynamically adjusted at mount time via `/etc/fstab` or `mount -o`:

```ini
# Production hardened, high-performance ext4 mount options
/dev/nvme0n1p2  /data  ext4  defaults,noatime,barrier=1,commit=30,errors=remount-ro  0 2
```

- **`noatime`**: Disables updating access timestamps on reads. Eliminates a write I/O for every file read, significantly boosting throughput and extending SSD lifespan.
- **`barrier=1`**: Enforces hardware write barriers (cache flushes) before committing JBD2 journal blocks. Prevents reordering of writes across volatile drive caches, ensuring zero corruption during power loss.
- **`commit=N`**: Sets the transaction commit interval in seconds (default is 5 seconds). Increasing to 30 seconds improves throughput by batching more writes, at the cost of losing up to 30 seconds of un-fsynced data after a crash.
- **`errors=remount-ro`**: If the kernel detects internal filesystem inconsistency or corrupted metadata, it immediately remounts the volume as strictly read-only, preventing corrupted structures from propagating further.

## Checking Feature Flags in Code

Systems software and diagnostic utilities can query feature flags by inspecting the superblock directly:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#define EXT4_MAGIC 0xEF53
#define EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_EXTENTS 0x0040
#define EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_64BIT   0x0080

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    int fd = open(argv[1], O_RDONLY);
    uint8_t sb[1024];

    /* Read superblock at byte offset 1024 */
    lseek(fd, 1024, SEEK_SET);
    read(fd, sb, 1024);

    uint16_t magic = *(uint16_t *)(sb + 0x38);
    if (magic != EXT4_MAGIC) {
        printf("Not a valid ext filesystem (magic: 0x%04X)\n", magic);
        return 1;
    }

    uint32_t incompat = *(uint32_t *)(sb + 0x60);
    printf("Superblock Magic: 0x%04X\n", magic);
    printf("Extents Enabled:   %s\n", (incompat & EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_EXTENTS) ? "YES" : "NO");
    printf("64-bit Addressing: %s\n", (incompat & EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_64BIT) ? "YES" : "NO");

    close(fd);
    return 0;
}
```

```bash
# Verify feature flags on the command line using tune2fs
sudo tune2fs -l /dev/nvme0n1p2 | grep "Filesystem features:"
```
